question: Mukund invests a sum of ₹5400 and Sachin invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Sachin gets ₹960 more interest than Mukund, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in Simple Interest for 5 years = ₹960

Difference in Simple Interest for 1 year = 960 ÷ 5 = ₹192

Rate % = (Interest difference for 1 year ÷ Difference in Principal) × 100

Rate % = (192 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 4.8%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal for Mukund (P₁) = ₹5400

Principal for Sachin (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 5 years
